correction.text: Rome and its immediate plain on both banks of the Tiber (one cell around 12.48 E 41.89 N, 15 km), from the founding of Rome in 753 BC

keyframe_review.note: 858.8 km2, bbox 11.97-12.45 E, 41.78-42.11 N. Corrected 2026-10-19 after review: this shape lies 95 percent on the right bank of the Tiber and holds Veii (12.40 E 42.02 N), not Rome (12.48 E 41.89 N, east of the shape's 12.452 E edge), Alba Longa (12.65 E) or Ostia (12.29 E 41.76 N); it is the ager Veientanus, which the Veii page puts 'between the right bank of the lower Tiber river and the coast' and which the etruscans dossier draws as Etruscan until 396. Rome is drawn instead as the city's plain around 12.48 E 41.89 N. Infobox: 'Founding of Rome: 753 BC' (Roman Kingdom page), three years before Cliopatria's 750. The page gives no area; the Roman expansion page says that at the Republic's birth Rome's 'possessions did not extend beyond 15 miles from the city', an upper bound of 24 km. The first stage is one 250 km2 cell of the grid, under the 859 km2 of Cliopatria's strip.

Servius Tullius and Tarquinius Superbus add no place the pages name ('conquered various Latin cities' is unplaced).

region.text: the city's plain around Rome (12.48 E 41.89 N), both banks of the Tiber, the Janiculum included

ledger.note: 753 BC: 'Founding of Rome: 753 BC' (infobox); Romulus the first king (753-716), who 'waged war with the Fidenates and Veientes and others'. Corrected 2026-10-19: the first run drew Cliopatria's 859 km2 'ager Romanus', which lies on the right bank and holds Veii, not Rome; the land is now the city's plain (15 km around Rome). The Kingdom page gives no area, no 'ager Romanus' figure and no distance.

region.text: Alba Longa in the Alban hills

ledger.note: 672 BC: Alba Longa. Under Tullus Hostilius (672-640) 'the city of Alba Longa was completely destroyed and Tullus integrated its population into Rome' (Roman Kingdom). Alba Longa page: destroyed 'around the middle of the 7th century BC', 'on Tullus' orders, the Roman soldiers demolished the 400-year-old city ... leaving only the temples standing'; the page gives no year (its infobox says 'Abandoned: c. 700 BC'); coordinates 41.7469 N 12.6503 E, in the Alban hills, which the first run wrongly held inside Cliopatria's shape. The year is the start of the reign; confidence 1. Mirror: latin-league /ledger/1 (loss -672).

640 BC: Ostia. Ancus Marcius (640-616) 'founded the port of Ostia Antica on the Tyrrhenian Sea' (Roman Kingdom). Ostia Antica page: legend credits Ancus Marcius, 'An inscription seems to confirm the establishment of the old castrum (military camp) of Ostia in the 7th century BC', but 'The oldest archaeological remains so far discovered date back to only the 4th century BC'; '25 km (16 mi) southwest of Rome', 41.756 N 12.292 E. The year is the start of the reign; confidence 1.

region.text: the Sabine-Latin towns north-east and east of Rome: Collatia, Crustumerium, Nomentum, Ficulea and their neighbours

ledger.note: 585 BC: Tarquinius Priscus' Sabine war. Priscus page: he held a triumph 'on 13 September 585 BC'; 'In the peace, Collatia was ceded to Rome'; after the Sabine victory 'Corniculum, Ficulea, Cameria, Crustumerium, Ameriola, Medullia, and Nomentum submitted to Roman administration'; the Latin war ('He captured the city of Apiolae by storm') was 'before 588 BC' and is unplaced. The Kingdom page says Priscus 'waged wars against the Sabines and Etruscans' and, in its table, 'Expanded Roman hegemony over Latium'; 'doubling the size of Rome' (Kingdom page; Priscus page makes no territorial claim). The year and the towns are the page's; the region (north-east and east of Rome, inside 15 miles) is my reading, the page gives no coordinates. Replaces the first run's 616 'gain from nobody' that moved no land. Mirror: sabines /ledger/1 puts a loss of the Roman bank north of the Anio to the Kingdom in 753 (confidence 1); the year differs.

ledger.note: 509 BC: 'Monarchy overthrown: 509 BC'. After Lucretia's death 'Lucius Junius Brutus led a revolt' that 'deposed and expelled Tarquinius and his family from Rome in 509 BC'; Brutus and Collatinus 'became Rome's first consuls, marking the beginning of the Roman Republic'. The alternative tradition (Tacitus, Pliny) that 'Porsena had actually captured Rome and imposed humiliating conditions' (508) is noted, not drawn.

wars.name: Wars of the Roman kings with Fidenae and Veii
wars.outcome: Roman victories in the tradition (Romulus, Tullus Hostilius, Servius Tullius' triumphs of 571 and 567); Priscus' Sabine war of 585 is the one dated war with named towns (gain 585); the Veii country stays Etruscan to 396
wars.note: The Roman-Etruscan Wars page's own infobox dates the wars from the 8th century BC, 'Location: Fidenae and Veii'.

certainty.note: Legendary period: the shape is a convention (the city's plain, then the places the pages name, within 15 miles of the city), not a frontier any page describes.

notes: Cliopatria's 'Roman Kingdom' row (-750..-481, three identical 858.8 km2 shapes) is a misplaced shape: 6 vertices, 11.97-12.45 E, 41.78-42.11 N, 95 percent west of the Tiber. It holds Veii and not Rome (12.48 E), Alba Longa (12.65 E) or Ostia; it is the ager Veientanus ('the entire region between the right bank of the lower Tiber river and the coast', Veii page), and the etruscans dossier draws that country as Etruscan until 396. The first run accepted it as the ager Romanus; the review of 2026-10-19 showed otherwise by point-in-polygon on the Cliopatria geometry. Corrected: dates re-set to the page's 753-509; the three Cliopatria shapes are marked wrong and the kingdom is drawn from the pages: the city's plain (one 250 km2 cell of the 15 km around Rome, both banks, the Janiculum included) from 753; Alba Longa's hills from 672 (reign of Tullus Hostilius, year = reign start, the Alba Longa page gives none); the Tiber-mouth cell of Ostia from 640 (reign of Ancus Marcius; the Ostia page: 7th-century castrum by an inscription, oldest remains 4th century); and the Sabine-Latin towns north-east of Rome from 585 (Priscus' triumph of 13 September 585 with Collatia ceded and seven towns submitted). Five cells (about 1,250 km2) at the end, inside the 15 miles (24 km) of the expansion page; Cliopatria's strip has 859 km2. The cell grid (about 250 km2 a cell) makes discs below 10 km a single cell. The first run's 616 'gain' of the already-held shape is dropped. Not drawn: Priscus' Latin war (Apiolae, before 588), Servius Tullius' Etruscan wars, Tarquinius Superbus' wars against the Volsci, Gabii and the Rutuli (unplaced on the pages). The Veii country is Etruscan until 396 and is not Roman. For the owners of other dossiers: roman-republic's -509 keyframe copies the misplaced strip and must be replaced by the land of FINAL (five cells around Rome); sabines /ledger/1 dates the Roman bank north of the Anio to 753 (here 585, from the Priscus page); latin-league's regions subtract the Cliopatria Roman Kingdom shape, which is not Rome. The rulers list is the page's seven kings. The shared Wikidata problem (Q175881 for the Republic) does not touch this row. Area: the page gives none; Cliopatria 858.8 km2 against 250 km2 at 753 and 1,250 km2 from 585.
